question: A 21-year-old man went to the emergency room after presenting several episodes of generalized tonic-clonic seizures in the last week. In the cranial CT scan, a unilocular cystic lesion was observed with a small nodule attached to the wall corresponding to the encysting larva of a parasite. Which of the following pathogens can be responsible ?:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Generalized tonic-clonic seizures" -> "Cranial CT scan shows unilocular cystic lesion" -> "Small nodule attached to cyst wall" -> "Encysting larva of a parasite" -> "Taenia solium" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Generalized tonic-clonic seizures" -> "Cranial CT scan shows unilocular cystic lesion" -> "Small nodule attached to cyst wall" -> "Neurocysticercosis" -> "Taenia solium" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Generalized tonic-clonic seizures" -> "Cranial CT scan shows unilocular cystic lesion" -> "Small nodule attached to cyst wall" -> "Parasitic infection" -> "Taenia solium" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Generalized tonic-clonic seizures" -> "Cranial CT scan shows unilocular cystic lesion" -> "Small nodule attached to cyst wall" -> "Possible parasitic infection" -> "Taenia solium" -> 80%
analysis: The clinical presentation and imaging findings are suggestive of neurocysticercosis, which is caused by the larval stage of Taenia solium. The presence of a unilocular cystic lesion with a nodule (scolex) is characteristic of this condition. Taenia saginata does not cause cysticercosis in humans, and the other options do not match the described imaging findings.
